title: llm-proxy configuration (v0)
description: The configuration format for llm-proxy. This file is the single source of truth for the v0 schema: user-facing documentation, editor autocomplete (yaml-language-server), and the config validator are all generated from it. Strings support environment-variable interpolation with `${VAR_NAME}`, applied before parsing. Parsing is strict: unknown fields are errors, never ignored. The top-level keys `envoy`, `tracing`, and `clusters` are RESERVED for future versions and rejected in v0.

version.description: Schema version. Must be 0. Future schema revisions bump this; llm-proxy refuses configs whose version it does not understand.

listen.description: Where the proxy accepts client traffic. Shorthand string `host:port`, or an object to enable TLS. Default: `0.0.0.0:8080` (plaintext).

admin.description: Admin/observability endpoint (`/ready`, `/config_dump`, `/clusters`, `/server_info`, `/stats`). `/stats` renders a flat text format, one `name: value` line per counter or histogram. Disabled when omitted. Bind to loopback unless you know why not.

auth.description: Downstream authentication: verifies inbound requests carry a known virtual key before any provider is reached. Fails CLOSED -- with this block present, a request with no recognized credential is refused (401), never admitted anonymously. Authorization is the opposite axis and defaults OPEN: an authenticated tenant with no configured policy may use every model and provider. Omit `auth` entirely to keep today's behavior (no application-level authentication).

providers.description: Named upstream LLM API providers. The key is the provider name referenced by `routes` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Names `openai`, `anthropic`, and `openrouter` infer their `type` and `base_url` automatically — a working OpenAI provider is just `openai: { api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} }`.

models.description: Logical model catalogue: a client-facing model name mapped to an ordered list of providers able to serve it -- e.g. Claude served by Anthropic directly or by Vertex, or Kimi-K2 served by Nebius. Each entry gets an implicit route matching its name, evaluated after `routes` and before the 404 backstop; `routes` still work unchanged. A key may be an exact model name, a single TRAILING wildcard (`gpt-4*`), or the bare catch-all `*` -- a `*` anywhere else (leading, mid-string, or more than one) is a load error, which is a narrower grammar than `routes[].model`'s (that one falls back to a general regex). Precedence when more than one key matches a request is total and exact match always wins, then the LONGEST matching prefix, then the bare `*` catch-all; two keys that could ever tie (a literal duplicate, since two distinct prefixes of equal length can never both match the same name) is a load error naming the duplicate. Today this is naming and data model only: only `providers[0]` is ever used to serve traffic, and every provider entry after the first produces a load-time warning naming its exact path instead of being silently accepted -- picking among them (fallback / weighted split / cost-aware) is not supported yet.

routes.description: Ordered routing rules, evaluated top to bottom — the FIRST rule whose `model` pattern matches the request wins (there is no specificity reordering; put specific patterns above broad ones). Requests matching no rule and no `models` entry get a 404 with a JSON error body listing known models.

limits.description: Rate limits and quotas. Today only `key: header:authorization` limits with `tokens_per_minute` set are actually enforced (a 429 with `x-ratelimit-*` headers before the request is forwarded; token counts are extracted from provider responses, streaming included, and an admitted request already in flight is never truncated). Every other combination -- `key: global`/`client-ip`, any other `header:<name>`, `requests_per_minute`, `concurrent_sessions`, `models` -- is recorded but not enforced yet, and produces a load-time warning naming the exact field. NOTE: limits are enforced PER PROXY INSTANCE in v0, and a fleet-wide token rate limit has no store to be enforced against. Do not read the shared `ControlPlaneStore` as covering this: it reconciles CURRENCY SPEND for the Envoy-mode `llmproxy.spend_limit` filter and holds no token-rate-limit counters. `auth.store` selects that same store type for minted keys and tenant policy only, and no `limits` entry reads it, so `auth.store: shared` does not make a token limit fleet-wide. Two replicas each admit up to `tokens_per_minute`.

observability.description: Metrics and access logging. Access logging is fully implemented, including token counts and TTFT/TPOT. Metrics are recorded and served on the admin endpoint at `/stats` and `/stats/prometheus`: per-cluster upstream request counts and an upstream request-time histogram. Two instruments are defined but NOT yet recorded and so never appear -- downstream connection counts, and GenAI token usage -- so do not build alerting on those two.

pricing.description: Versioned LLM model rate card. Each completed request is priced in integer nanodollars using all four token buckets. Updating a file source requires config reload.

HostPort.description: A bind address in `host:port` form. IPv6 hosts use brackets: `[::1]:8080`.

Duration.description: A duration: integer plus unit — `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), or `h` (hours).

TokenAmount.description: A token count: a plain integer, or a string with `k` (thousands) / `m` (millions) suffix.

ModelPattern.description: A glob matched against the request's `model` field (the JSON body field for chat/completions APIs; the `model` query parameter for realtime WebSocket endpoints). `*` matches any run of characters; matching is case-sensitive. `*` alone matches every request.

ProviderModelRef.description: A provider reference: `provider-name` (keep the request's model name) or `provider-name/model-name` (rewrite the model before forwarding, e.g. fall back from `gpt-5` to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`).

tls.description: Terminate TLS for client connections. Certificate files are read once at startup; a renewed certificate needs a restart to be served. The hot-swap mechanism exists internally but nothing watches the files yet, so do not plan renewal around it.

cert_file.description: Path to the PEM certificate chain.

key_file.description: Path to the PEM private key.

Auth.description: Downstream authentication. Exactly one of `hmac_secret` / `hmac_secret_file` is required -- mirrors the `api_key`/`api_key_file` choice on a `Provider`.

hmac_secret.description: The operator secret that keys the HMAC over virtual-key digests. Use `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation rather than inlining it.

hmac_secret_file.description: Read the HMAC secret from this file (trailing whitespace trimmed; read once at startup -- hot reload is not supported yet).

keys.description: Configured virtual keys. May be empty -- an `auth:` block with no keys authenticates nothing and therefore refuses every request (the correct fail-closed reading of "authentication is enabled, and no credential is valid"), which is legal but almost certainly a mistake, so it produces a load-time warning.

store.description: Where minted keys, revocations, and tenant policy live. Absent means `in_memory`, which keeps them only for the life of the process. Exactly one of the three shapes below, the same three the Envoy-mode `llmproxy.auth` filter accepts. The store is fixed at startup: changing it takes a restart, not a `SIGHUP` reload.

in_memory.description: Keys and policy live only for the life of the process. Takes no fields.

AuthStorePersistent.description: Keys and policy survive a restart in an embedded `redb` file. The file is created if missing and takes a lock, so one process owns it at a time.

AuthStoreShared.description: Keys and policy are shared by every replica through Redis. Exactly one of `url` / `url_file` is required -- a Redis URL may embed a password, so it belongs in the environment or a mounted file, same as `hmac_secret`.

url.description: The Redis connection URL, e.g. `redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@host:6379/0`. Use `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation rather than inlining a password.

url_file.description: Read the Redis URL from this file (trailing whitespace trimmed; read once at startup).

namespace.description: Prefixes every Redis key this store touches, so two deployments can share one Redis. Unset or empty uses the built-in default, `llmproxy`.

AuthKey.description: One virtual key. The plaintext key never appears in configuration -- only a keyed digest of it.

id.description: Names this credential in audit logs and in the access log's response-code details. Must be unique within `auth.keys`.

tenant.description: The tenant (account/team) this key authenticates as. Several keys may share a tenant; that's the normal case -- revoking one leaked key must not revoke the whole account.

digest.description: Lowercase hex of `HMAC-SHA256(hmac_secret, <plaintext key>)`, exactly 64 characters -- the plaintext is shown to the operator once, at creation, and is never recoverable from configuration. Generate both together with `llm-proxy --mode keygen --tenant <tenant> --key-id <id>` (reads the same secret via `--hmac-secret-file`/`$LLMPROXY_AUTH_SECRET`, and prints a ready-to-paste `id`/`tenant`/`digest` block). If you have no `llm-proxy` binary handy, `openssl` computes the same digest (note `printf %s`, not a here-string -- `<<<` appends a trailing newline that changes the digest): `printf %s "llmp_yourkey" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$LLMPROXY_AUTH_SECRET" -hex`

revoked.description: A revoked key is refused, distinguished from an unknown key in the access log's response-code details (`auth_revoked_key` vs `auth_unknown_key`) but NOT on the wire -- both produce an identical 401, so a caller can't learn from the response alone whether a key they guessed was ever valid.

Provider.description: One upstream LLM API. Exactly one of `api_key` / `api_key_file` may be set (omit both for unauthenticated local backends). Azure OpenAI requires `deployment` and `api_version`; Vertex requires project, location, publisher, and one OAuth access-token source; Bedrock requires region and AWS access-key and secret-key sources.

type.description: Provider API shape. `openrouter` uses OpenAI-compatible requests with cluster-owned /v1 to /api/v1 path rewriting. `openai-compatible` covers vLLM, Ollama, TGI, Together, and most self-hosted servers. Inferred for providers named `openai`, `anthropic`, or `openrouter`; defaults to `openai-compatible` otherwise. `azure-openai` uses Azure's deployment URL and `api-version` query parameter. `vertex` uses Google Cloud project/location/publisher settings and an OAuth access token. `bedrock` uses an AWS region and SigV4 credential sources.

base_url.description: API base URL. Required unless the provider name/type implies one (`openai` -> https://api.openai.com, `anthropic` -> https://api.anthropic.com, `openrouter` -> https://openrouter.ai).

deployment.description: Azure OpenAI deployment name. Required for `azure-openai`; used as a path segment.

api_version.description: Azure OpenAI API version query value. Required for `azure-openai`; sent as `api-version`.

api_key.description: API key, sent using provider type's native auth header (`api-key` for Azure OpenAI, `Authorization: Bearer` for other OpenAI-shaped APIs, `x-api-key` for Anthropic). Use `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation rather than inlining secrets.

api_key_file.description: Read the API key from this file (trailing whitespace trimmed; read once at startup -- hot reload is not supported yet). Preferred over `api_key` for secret managers that mount files.

project.description: Google Cloud project ID for Vertex AI. Required for `vertex`; rejected for other provider types.

location.description: Google Cloud location for Vertex AI. Required for `vertex`; rejected for other provider types.

publisher.description: Vertex AI publisher, such as `google` or `anthropic`. Required for `vertex`; rejected for other provider types.

access_token.description: OAuth access token for Vertex AI. Exactly one of `access_token` / `access_token_file` is required for `vertex`.

access_token_file.description: Read the Vertex OAuth access token from this file. Exactly one of `access_token` / `access_token_file` is required for `vertex`.

region.description: AWS region for Amazon Bedrock. Required for `bedrock`; rejected for other provider types.

access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID for Bedrock SigV4. Exactly one of `access_key_id` / `access_key_id_file` is required for `bedrock`.

access_key_id_file.description: Read the AWS access key ID from this file. Exactly one of `access_key_id` / `access_key_id_file` is required for `bedrock`.

secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key for Bedrock SigV4. Exactly one of `secret_access_key` / `secret_access_key_file` is required for `bedrock`.

secret_access_key_file.description: Read the AWS secret access key from this file. Exactly one of `secret_access_key` / `secret_access_key_file` is required for `bedrock`.

session_token.description: Optional AWS session token for Bedrock SigV4. If set, do not set `session_token_file`.

session_token_file.description: Read an optional AWS session token from this file. If set, do not set `session_token`.

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to send on every request to this provider (e.g. org/project headers). Anthropic providers are sent a default `anthropic-version` automatically; setting it here overrides that default (header names are matched case-insensitively).

ca_file.description: PEM CA bundle for verifying this provider's TLS certificate. Only needed for self-hosted backends with private CAs; system roots are used otherwise.

connect_timeout.description: TCP/TLS connection establishment timeout for this provider.

protocol.description: Upstream HTTP protocol for this provider's cluster. `http2` enables upstream connection reuse: the proxy keeps one multiplexed connection per worker to this provider instead of connecting fresh on every request. Most hosted providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, and most OpenAI-compatible APIs) support it; many local/self-hosted plaintext servers do not. Defaults to `http1`.

ModelDef.description: One logical model and the providers able to serve it.

providers.description: Providers tried for this model, in priority order. Each entry is either the shorthand string form (`provider` or `provider/model`, reusing the same `ProviderModelRef` shape `routes` uses) or the object form, needed whenever `dialect` must be set explicitly. Only `providers[0]` is used to serve traffic today -- every later entry is validated at load time (a bad one still fails to load) but produces a load-time warning naming its exact path instead of being selected; choosing among them is not supported yet.

ModelProvider.description: The object form of a `models.<name>.providers` entry, needed whenever `dialect` must be explicit -- the shorthand string form (`provider` or `provider/model`) cannot carry it.

model.description: Upstream model ID at this provider, if different from the model's own catalogue name (e.g. Anthropic's dated model IDs, or a Vertex publisher-model path). Recorded; substituting it into the request body needs a request-body rewriter, which is not supported yet, so this produces a load-time warning until then and the client's original model name is forwarded as-is.

dialect.description: Wire format this provider entry speaks. Optional (and derived from the provider's `type`) for `openai`/`anthropic`/`openai-compatible`/`azure-openai`, whose wire format the type alone determines. REQUIRED for `vertex`/`bedrock`, which serve more than one wire format under a single provider type -- e.g. Vertex hosts Anthropic-shaped Claude, Google-shaped Gemini, and OpenAI-shaped Kimi. Omitting it there is a load error naming the field, never a guess: the wrong parser can partially match the wrong body shape and bill usage against a number nobody computed. The shorthand string form cannot express this field at all, so an ambiguous-type provider used here must use this object form.

provider.description: Where matching requests go. `provider/model` form rewrites the model name before forwarding.

fallbacks.description: Tried in order when the primary provider fails (connection failure, 429, or 5xx — and never after the first response byte of a stream has been sent to the client). Each fallback gets a fresh attempt with the same request body, model-rewritten if the `provider/model` form is used.

retries.description: Retry policy for this route. Defaults are LLM-safe: retry only what is certainly unserved (connection failures, 429s, and 5xx received before any response byte); a request is never replayed once streaming to the client has begun. NOT a separate budget from `fallbacks` -- both draw on one retry count, and each retry against a fallback chain moves to the NEXT member rather than repeating the primary.

attempts.description: Extra attempts (0 disables retries). On a route with `fallbacks`, retries walk the chain instead of repeating the primary, and the emitted retry count is raised to whichever is larger -- this value, or the number needed to reach the last fallback -- so 0 does NOT disable failover there.

idle_timeout.description: Maximum time with NO bytes flowing (between response chunks / SSE events / WebSocket frames). There is deliberately no total-duration timeout by default — LLM generations and realtime sessions are long-lived; idle-based timeouts are the correct guard.

streaming.description: Assert that every configured HTTP filter for this route flushes response bytes through. Configuration loading fails if any installed filter can buffer a response; omit this field for the normal streaming-by-default behavior.

key.description: What the limit is counted against: `global` (one bucket for all traffic), `client-ip` (one bucket per client address), `tenant` (one bucket per authenticated tenant -- requires an `auth:` block; configuring this without one is a load error, since nothing would authenticate a tenant), or `header:<name>` (one bucket per distinct value of the named request header — e.g. `header:x-api-key` for per-caller quotas). `header:authorization` and `tenant` are enforced today (the token limiter's bucket key is hardcoded to the `authorization` header, but automatically prefers the authenticated tenant instead whenever `auth:` is configured -- so a `header:<name>` limit alongside `auth:` produces a not-enforced-as-written warning suggesting `key: tenant`). `global`, `client-ip`, and every other `header:<name>` without `auth:` are recorded but produce a not-enforced warning.

tokens_per_minute.description: Total (input + output) tokens allowed per minute per bucket. Usage is extracted from provider responses, including streamed ones; enforcement is at request admission (the request that would exceed the budget is rejected — in-flight streams are never truncated). Enforced only when paired with `key: header:authorization`; any other key still records this field but produces a not-enforced warning instead.

requests_per_minute.description: Requests allowed per minute per bucket. Not enforced yet by any key -- the current limiter enforces total token budgets, not a request-rate cap (a different feature); recorded, and produces a not-enforced warning.

concurrent_sessions.description: Maximum simultaneous long-lived sessions (WebSocket realtime connections and active SSE streams) per bucket. Enforced at connection/upgrade time — the 429 happens before the session starts, never mid-session. Not enforced yet; recorded, and produces a not-enforced warning.

models.description: Restrict this limit to requests whose model matches one of these patterns. Omit to apply to all traffic. Not enforced yet -- the current limiter has no per-model scoping; recorded, and produces a not-enforced warning.

access_logs.description: Where and how per-request/per-session access log entries are written.

output.description: `stdout`, `stderr`, or a file path. Streamed responses and realtime sessions are logged once at stream end with usage totals.

format.description: `json` emits one structured object per line (recommended for log pipelines).

force_usage_reporting.description: Forces `stream_options.include_usage` onto streaming OpenAI-dialect requests that didn't already ask for it, so token usage can be logged/accounted for streamed responses. This makes the provider emit one extra final SSE frame carrying usage; well-behaved SDKs handle it, but a hand-rolled client that iterates `choices[0]` without a guard can trip over that frame. Set to `false` for strict passthrough if that's a concern.

metrics.description: OTLP metric export. Independent of `tracing`: set this without `tracing` to export metrics with tracing fully off, and note that turning tracing off does not stop metrics. Omit entirely for no OTLP metric export -- which does not disable `/stats/prometheus`, which works with no OTLP configuration at all. `export_deadline` must be shorter than `export_interval`, or every export is abandoned as a timeout before the next one is due.

otlp_endpoint.description: The OTLP/gRPC collector endpoint for metrics. May differ from the tracing one.

export_interval.description: How often to snapshot and export the registry. Each export is a full cumulative snapshot, so this trades collector bandwidth against freshness. Bounded to 1s-1h.

export_deadline.description: Per-export deadline. This is what bounds a collector that accepts a connection and then stops responding, rather than merely retrying it. Must be less than `export_interval`.

tracing.description: OTLP trace export: config surface only -- nothing exports a span yet. Omit entirely to keep tracing off. An inbound `traceparent`'s sampled bit is always honored regardless of `sample_ratio`; the ratio only applies when this proxy mints a new root span.

export_deadline.description: Per-export deadline for trace-batch RPCs. Bounds a collector that accepts the connection and then stops responding: each hung attempt costs one timeout, never an indefinite stall. Bounded to 100ms-60s.

sample_ratio.description: Head-sampling ratio for a newly minted root span (no inbound `traceparent`, or one that arrives unsampled).

catalog.description: Public source pricing metadata exposed by the admin pricing inventory; never used as token rates.

version.description: Human label; recorded version includes a content hash.

cached_input_unpriced.description: Requests reporting cached input remain unpriced.

cache_write_unpriced.description: Requests reporting cache creation remain unpriced.
